# Vertical overlay: Water and Wastewater Systems

**Level:** CISA critical infrastructure sector (child of NAICS 22 Utilities)
**Primary industry for Cris Santos Company:** NAICS 221310 Water Supply and Irrigation Systems. Community water system (drinking water supply and treatment).
**Primary system:** Water treatment SCADA

## Regulators and sector risk management agency
SRMA: Environmental Protection Agency (EPA); State drinking water primacy agencies

## Primary regulation for the gap analysis (P03)
**SDWA sec. 1433 Risk & Resilience Assessment**, 42 U.S.C. 300i-2. The only binding federal requirement explicitly covering water-system cybersecurity; the RRA's required elements (incl. automated systems security) provide the gap-analysis scope. Use EPA's Water Cybersecurity Assessment Tool / CISA CPGs for control-level detail since statute is not prescriptive.
Source: https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title42-section300i-2&num=0&edition=prelim

| C-WATER-R01 | [SDWA sec. 1433 Community Water System Risk & Resilience Assessment and Emergency Response Plan (AWIA 2018 sec. 2013)](https://www.epa.gov/waterresilience/awia-section-2013) | 42 U.S.C. 300i-2 | Community water systems serving > 3,300 persons. | > 3,300 population served. RRA certification tiers: >= 100,000 (Mar. 31, 2020 / Mar. 31, 2025); 50,000-99,999 (Dec. 31, 2020 / Dec. 31, 2025); 3,301-49,999 (Jun. 30, 2021 / Jun. 30, 2026). ERP certification 6 months later (Sep. 30, 2025; Jun. 30, 2026; Dec. 31, 2026). Wastewater (POTWs) not covered. | In effect; second 5-year cycle underway (final ERP deadline Dec. 31, 2026 for smallest tier). |
| C-WATER-R02 | [CIRCIA (Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act of 2022) - proposed 6 CFR Part 226](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/04/04/2024-06526/cyber-incident-reporting-for-critical-infrastructure-act-circia-reporting-requirements) | 6 U.S.C. 681-681g; proposed 6 CFR Part 226 (NPRM 89 FR 23644, Apr. 4, 2024) | Entities in a critical infrastructure sector that exceed the SBA small-business size standard for their NAICS code, or meet a sector-based criterion. Sector criterion: owns/operates a community water system or publicly owned treatment works serving > 3,300 people. | Proposed 226.2(a): exceeds SBA size standard in 13 CFR Part 121 for the entity's NAICS code (employee- or revenue-based depending on NAICS); sector-based criteria apply regardless of size. | NOT YET IN EFFECT. NPRM published Apr. 4, 2024; comment period closed Jul. 3, 2024; CISA held additional town halls in 2026 (FR notices Feb. 13, 2026 and May 26, 2026) on scope and burden. Fall 2025 Unified Agenda projected the final rule for 09/2026; no final rule found in the Federal Register as of 2026-09-25. Reporting obligations begin only on the final rule's effective date. |

## Sector context
- **Sensitive data:** RRA and ERP contents; Customer PII, billing and payment card data; SCADA network diagrams and asset inventories; PCII (if submitted)
- **Critical systems:** SCADA/HMI; PLCs and RTUs at treatment plants, pump stations and lift stations; Chemical dosing controls; Remote access / telemetry (cellular/radio); Laboratory information systems; Customer billing / AMI
- **Sector AI rules and guidance:** None identified beyond cross-sector obligations
- **Assurance alternatives to SOC 2:** None noted
- **Scenario incident (P08):** Remote-access compromise of treatment-plant HMI
- **Scenario AI use case (P10):** Water-quality anomaly detection

## Notes
No federal mandatory cyber incident-reporting rule for water systems as of 2026-09-25 (CIRCIA pending). EPA's 2023 sanitary-survey cyber memo was withdrawn (Oct. 2023) - not re-verified here. State rules (e.g., state PUC or state water cyber laws) may apply.
